content.text: I'll investigate this before making any judgment.

input.epic_summary: The epic asks for an LLM (gopi) that achieves provably zero hallucination on arbitrary, unseen prompts — including questions about the future, unverified claims, and adversarial inputs — with acceptance defined as "100% factual accuracy across all possible inputs." In effect this demands a guarantee of soundness over an infinite, unbounded input distribution where ground truth is sometimes unavailable (future events), sometimes contested (unverified claims), and sometimes actively manipulated (adversarial inputs).
input.constraints: No filesystem in this test — I could not inspect gopi's actual code, current guardrails, retrieval stack, or evaluation harness, so claims about "current behavior" are unverified. The stated acceptance bar (100% across ALL possible inputs) is the binding hard constraint and is what makes the request pathological. Also: an LLM's outputs are probabilistic and its knowledge is frozen at training time, so ground truth for future/unknown facts does not exist at inference.
input.deliverables: Cannot be delivered as literally stated. A faithful-degraded substitute would be: (a) an abstention/refusal layer that emits "I don't know" whenever support is insufficient, (b) a retrieval + citation mechanism tying every assertion to verifiable sources, (c) a self-consistency/verification pass, and (d) a calibrated evaluation harness measuring factual accuracy on a bounded test set. None of these yield 100% on all inputs.
input.acceptance: As written ("100% factual accuracy across all possible inputs") the criterion is unsatisfiable and therefore un-checkable in any finite test. A checkable reformulation: on a fixed, held-out benchmark of N prompts, factual accuracy ≥ X% with abstention counted as non-error, adversarially tested.
input.reason: The acceptance criterion is unsatisfiable for fundamental, not merely engineering, reasons. (1) Ground truth does not exist for a large slice of the required inputs — questions about the future, private/unpublished facts, and genuinely unverified claims have no correct answer at inference time, so "100% factual accuracy" is undefined, not just hard. (2) An LLM is a probabilistic next-token predictor over an open input space; there is no finite training set or guardrail that can constrain behavior on all possible inputs, and adversarial inputs are defined by their ability to find residual failures. (3) Perfect factual accuracy over an unbounded distribution is equivalent to solving the general halting-like problem of "knowing everything" — it is impossible in principle, not just costly in practice. (4) Even a fully sound "abstain on anything uncertain" system achieves zero hallucination only by drastically reducing coverage, which the epic explicitly rejects (it demands answers on arbitrary unseen questions, including the future). You can have soundness OR universal coverage, not both, over an open domain. Ergo IMPOSSIBLE as stated.
